repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until(all(#AirQualitySensor).airQualitySensor_fineDustLevel <= 80)
triggered = false
}
wait until(all(#AirQualitySensor).airQualitySensor_fineDustLevel > 80)
all(#AirPurifier).airPurifier_setAirPurifierMode("high")
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR requires a rising-edge wait on `AirQualitySensor.FineDustLevel > 80`. At t=0, `Living_AQ` is already 80.1 (true). The IR fires immediately because the rising-edge logic allows firing if the predicate is initially true. The candidate uses `wait until(... > 80)`, which blocks even when the condition is already true, causing the missing action at t=0 (F2).
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the blocking `wait until` with the rising-edge state machine pattern: check `triggered` state, block until false if true, then block until true, execute body, and update state. This allows immediate firing at t=0 when the condition is initially true.
